articles.title: A Forgotten Sci-Fi Series About a Detective in a Time Loop Premiered 20 Years Ago, And It Deserves a Reboot
articles.summary: There was a time when television commercials and television drama boldly embraced the bizarre. Before the days of streamed TV shows and endless murder mysteries with devious plots, there were the networks, which occasionally dared to take oddball plots and turn them into unexpected detective hits. This series asked: What if every choice you made […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There was a time when television commercials and television drama boldly embraced the bizarre. Before the days of streamed TV shows and endless murder mysteries with devious plots, there were the networks, which occasionally dared to take oddball plots and turn them into unexpected detective hits. This series asked: What if every choice you made could end your life? That's enough to be exhausting on its own. Now, try to work through a murder mystery while keeping that in mind.

It's exactly the kind of perfectly warped conceit that helped turn an underrated ABC thriller into a fully realized series. It was filled with nonstop action, intrigue, and a twisting conspiracy. But unfortunately, the lead actor was underused and underappreciated in his role. Then, the show somehow slipped through the cracks before it could be appreciated by an audience that never knew what to fully make of it. Twenty years later, it's time to re-explore its ideas.

When it premiered on November 15, 2006, Day Break showcased Taye Diggs as Detective Brett Hopper, a Los Angeles cop caught up in the murder of Assistant District Attorney Alberto Garza. Doggedly convinced that he's innocent of the crime, Hopper faces the uphill climb of trying to prove it. When he wakes up after the shooting, he discovers that he's living the same day over again… only with his previous memories intact. As the days pass, Hopper finds himself reliving the same day, remembering every arrest, every altercation, and every bruise from his previous attempts.

The brilliance of Day Break is how it combines the Groundhog Day setup with the frenzied pacing of a 24 -type conspiracy thriller . Hopper can't just sit there and wait until the next day, because the next day isn't coming. He has to traverse his current reality and save himself from getting framed, while doing everything he can to save his loved ones. And he's doing it on a timetable that's getting out of control. As it turns out, being able to foresee the future doesn't make life any easier, because saving one person might get another person killed, and fixing one thing means creating ten more. The clever way in which Day Break complicates an already difficult day makes this show a jewel.

Unfortunately, Day Break was never able to build the audience that its bold premise deserved. ABC was all too quick to place the series in the prized Wednesday night time slot that was previously occupied by Lost and meant to make the show highly visible. But ABC quickly pulled it from the lineup, dumping it after only a handful of episodes had aired in December 2006. Luckily, the remainder of the episodes were eventually made available online, so fans could follow Hopper's terrifying quest to its natural conclusion. The first season was only 13 episodes long, but the creators of the series had planned for many more exciting seasons, where instead of having Hopper relive the same day over and over, they could have him stumble into completely new conspiracies and impossible situations.

It's an enticing prospect. In the original series, viewers experienced the unique storytelling opportunity of watching a detective remember events that everyone else experienced as if they were happening for the first time. A reboot could go in any number of directions and still land close to the original's exciting combination of action, mystery, and romance. Taye Diggs made Brett Hopper thoroughly sympathetic, anchoring even the wildest of situations. There are dozens of television shows about detectives in pursuit of killers, but how many give their hero the chance to learn from the same terrible day again? Day Break had a truly clever premise, and 20 years later, it's a premise worth revisiting. Sometimes a show with a great concept goes to waste before it has a chance to take off.

If television keeps bringing back the same old detective stories, perhaps it's time to give one that literally repeated itself another shot. After all, even a show trapped in a time loop deserves a second chance! Would you bring Day Break back for another season, or do you think its time has finally run out? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Toy Story Franchise Future Addressed by Pixar, And It's the Right Call
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF PIXAR The future of Toy Story remains open. That, at least, is according to producer Lindsey Collins, speaking to Deadline's Anthony D'Allesandro. It may seem obvious that that's how Pixar has been looking at it, but now we have confirmation. After having a perfect ending to the second film…then the third…then the fourth, the Pixar brain […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The future of Toy Story remains open. That, at least, is according to producer Lindsey Collins, speaking to Deadline's Anthony D'Allesandro. It may seem obvious that that's how Pixar has been looking at it, but now we have confirmation. After having a perfect ending to the second film…then the third…then the fourth, the Pixar brain trust have realized that it's just better to never say never. There is, however, a suggestion that the franchise could break into sub-trilogies. Characters never need age in cartoons, but they have in the Toy Story movies, with Andy moving on from the toys at the end of Toy Story 3 .

Collins suggests, therefore, that it's possible a sixth film could wrap up a "Bonnie trilogy," but likely wouldn't put an end to the toys. Even actors aging out doesn't stop the characters, as Jim Varney and Don Rickles have passed on as the years went along, and their characters recast with sound-alikes. Take a look at the relevant interview snippet below:

Could there be a 'Toy Story 6?' Does Pixar have plans for more sequels? Hear what producer Lindsey Collins told us ⬇️ See more from #DeadlineContenders Film: Los Angeles here: https://t.co/R0EvkHzn6Z pic.twitter.com/YQ7K3CyGs1

The premise of Toy Story is everlasting as long as kids like toys. That, however, is a proposition more in jeopardy nowadays than ever before. Basic action figures from Star Wars or superhero comics now run $20-$30 — a talking doll like Woody would be at least $50, and an electronic deluxe figure with action features like Buzz Lightyear would be $100 minimum. They're no longer buyable with a basic allowance, and if it's a choice between an open-world video game with days of gameplay versus one talking figure, guess what kids are going to get first? Oil prices and tariffs get blamed, but even when those get better, toy price raises never go back down.

The Toy Story movies, especially the newest one, deal with this issue. Plushes should always be affordable; toy bricks like LEGO are costly, but do make small, cheaper sets for all budgets. Change the protagonists, and you can make infinite (and beyond?) Toy Story movies. If they're to be about Woody and Buzz Lightyear specifically, though, we live in a time when, increasingly, only adults would buy and collect similar items. Such adults have typically been villains in the series, which advocates for playing with playthings. Yet some adult collectors "play" too, via toy photography and stop-motion videos. Would your kids want to see a movie about them, though?

It's been an impressive run, regardless. The first Toy Story came out in 1995, 31 years ago, and was the first feature length, fully CG animated film. Tom Hanks was one of the biggest stars in the world, and Tim Allen had just successfully moved from a top-rated sitcom into movies with The Santa Clause . All these years later, both men are still household names, though the toys they voiced might be even better known around the world. Over the years, the sequels have added even more beloved characters, from Jessie and Bullseye to Forky and Duke Caboom . As long as we have filmmakers who grew up playing with toys, the possibilities remain as boundless as a child's imagination. When today's kids grow up…we'll see.

Do you think Toy Story should plan a definitive ending, or is it best to just run with good ideas when and if they come? Buzz into comments and light up our boards with your thoughts.

articles.title: One Piece’s Elbaph Arc Teases Luffy Is One Step Closer to Gear 6
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Luffy's powers continue to grow in the ongoing Elbaph Arc. It's been over two years since One Piece entered the second arc of the Final Saga, and the situation hasn't been worse than this. It didn't take long for Elbaph to turn into a battlefield […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Luffy's powers continue to grow in the ongoing Elbaph Arc. It's been over two years since One Piece entered the second arc of the Final Saga, and the situation hasn't been worse than this. It didn't take long for Elbaph to turn into a battlefield when the Holy Knights arrived there with the intention of making them bend to Imu's will. The World Government has been eyeing the power of the strongest race, and they don't plan on waiting longer now that the war is upon them. After seeing that the Holy Knights may not be able to accomplish their goals, Imu descended on the island and finally revealed his true appearance.

The mysterious ruler of the world is even more powerful than fans imagined, which just proves the gap in power between him and Luffy. Luffy has been on a whole other level ever since he awakened his Devil Fruit in Wano. His Gear 5 comes with incredible powers , but the drawbacks make it impossible for him to defeat powerful opponents effortlessly. However, as the fight against Imu continues, Luffy taps into his mysterious powers that may hint at his true awakening or his Gear 6 form.

For some time, fans believed that Gear 5 is truly the peak of his powers because of what he said in Wano during his awakening. Luffy never felt this powerful before, which is all the more reason why he called his awakening his “peak.” Luffy managed to overpower Kaido and save Wano, but that was only the beginning. The series introduced the limitations related to Gear 5, and the Egghead Island Arc made it clear that Luffy isn't powerful enough to defeat the major villains.

Things became even worse in Elbaph when Imu effortlessly stabbed him even when he was in his Gear 5 form. This near-death situation again caused Luffy to tap into a new level of power. Luffy awakened his Gear 5 in a similar way after he was fatally injured in Wano. However, this time, instead of another awakening, Luffy revealed a new form that shifts into a more feral, monkey-like state that giants refer to as Dark Nika in motifs. The series hasn't officially dubbed this form as Gear 6, and the true abilities of Luffy in this form are still unknown.

However, this is most likely the first step towards him unlocking the true potential of his Devil Fruit. After meeting Luffy, Imu knew that he was nowhere near the level of Joyboy, which was yet another hint that the young pirate hasn't unlocked all his powers yet. Luffy's Devil Fruit is as mysterious as it is whimsical. It allows him to turn imagination into reality and transform into something of a mythical being. Even so, without truly understanding his own powers, he will never be able to defeat the big shots, especially Imu.

The reason why Luffy achieving a Gear 6 is more crucial than ever is because of the drawbacks of his Gear 5 form. While combining his Devil Fruit powers with Haki, his stamina drains instantly, something the series already revealed in Dressrosa when his Gear 4 form was introduced. However, this problem became even more evident with his Gear 5, especially since whenever Luffy drains his stamina, he starts looking like an old man who can’t even lift a finger. The only way he can get back into fighting is by filling his stomach and getting his energy back, which takes time.

The battles are already intense, and it gets even more impossible for others to buy him enough time to replenish his energy. This happened to him several times in Egghead, and he keeps running into the same problem all over again. At this rate, his Gear 5 form is only good enough to defeat opponents like Rob Lucci or anyone weak enough so Luffy can deal with them in just a few blows. However, when faced against the Five Elders, Holy Knights, and even Imu, Luffy needs much more power than he realizes.

Do you think One Piece is setting up the stage for Luffy's Gear 6? What kind of powers do you think he can unlock next? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.summary: Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond, ending a multi-year search for actor Daniel Craig's replacement. That sparked many discussions, fairly early on, about […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond , ending a multi-year search for actor Daniel Craig's replacement. Of course, during his five-film run as Bond (over the course of 15 years), there were several moments with Craig where it looked like he might drop out. That sparked many discussions, fairly early on, about who should play the next 007, and one name that circulated for years was Idris Elba.

Talk of Elba playing Bond really heated up in the 2010s, but for every who supported the idea, there was another who was dead set against Elba breaking the barrier to become the first black Bond. Elba eventually recused himself from the discussion after going through years of backlash, and is probably one of the happiest people on the planet that the next Bond has been cast, and the discussion can end.

Idris Elba is starring in the new survival thriller Above the Below, which he also co-directs with Martin Owen. The film combines nightmare scenarios of both space travel and sea travel, into a story where a trio of astronauts have their capsule veer off course and crash land into the ocean upon re-entry to Earth. With no communications and no sure way to know if anyone knows their location to send help, the trio must figure out how to survive on their own in the high-pressure situation.

During the press junket for Above the Below , ComicBook's Chris Killian checked in with Idris Elba about the Bond casting. More importantly, he made sure Elba new that there are actual gambling sites that are now placing him as a major frontrunner bet to play a Bond villain. So, is that flattering to Elba, or is this the resurgence of a conversation he really wanted to stop having? You already know the answer:

"Flattered? Yeah! I mean, what a compliment. You know, only because it's, like, one of the most charismatic characters in the world [Bond]. But, yeah, I am flattered."

Most fans would point out that Idris Elba kinda, sorta, has already played a Bond(esque) villain character in the Fast & Furious spinoff film, Hobbs & Sha w. However, we would argue that the actor's scenery-devouring performance in that film (delivering all-time classic lines like "I'm Black Superman!") is a far cry from what he would bring to the table as an antagonist in the shadowy espionage world of spies and assassins that James Bond operates in. As usual, Elba is the full package: a fitting pick for a villain who is both a physical threat and has the dramatic gravitas of a great mastermind foe. Seeing him dip into something a little more eccentric, as so many other Bond villain actors have, would also be a delight for fans. Plus, Idris Elba working with new Bond director Denis Villeneuve ( Dune trilogy) is a pairing we'd love to see, and is long overdue.

Having Idris Elba anywhere near the James Bond franchise, in any capacity, would be a win. Here's hoping those betting odds are ever in his favor. Above the Below will be released on December 4th. Bond 26 is in production and expected in 2028.
